scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

Now, where I live, if you don't get rid of your stuff when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove it, and that cost comes out of your deposit. I've heard of people losing $250 because of this. So, I tried to contact him for two weeks, texting and emailing, asking him to pick up his stuff or let me take them to the dump. But he never responded. I ended up taking most of his stuff to the dump, but he had around 60 video games for the PS4. I thought, why not sell them? There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Fast forward to last week, I saw him at a party, and we were being polite. He asked how the move-out process went, and I told him it was good. Then he asked what I did with his stuff. When he found out I sold his games, he got mad. I told him I tried to reach out to him to get his stuff, but he never responded. Now he's calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing wrong with what I did. But now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for selling his games without his permission. Hmm, so the main issue here is whether I was right to sell his games without his consent. On one hand, I tried to contact him, and he didn't respond. Did it say anything about what happens to belongings left behind? If it didn't, then legally, I might be in the clear. But morally, is it right to sell someone's stuff without their okay? Also, considering the cost of having his stuff removed versus selling the games for $600, it seems like I saved him money by selling the games instead of having his deposit docked. But he's still upset because I sold his property without his permission. Maybe I should have handled it differently. Perhaps I could have stored his games somewhere and waited longer for him to respond, or maybe I could have offered to give him the money if he wanted to keep the games. But I didn't think of that at the time. In the end, even though I didn't break any laws, I might have made a mistake by selling his games without his consent. I think there's a part of me that is, because I didn't get his explicit permission to sell his games. Even though I tried to reach out, not getting a response doesn't necessarily give me the right to dispose of his belongings. I should probably apologize for selling his games without his consent and maybe offer to give him some of the money from the sale or return the games if he still wants them.
